title: Three-phase commit · recover an interrupted transfer
summary: A transfer spans two or more ledger shards. The coordinator can disappear between any two message deliveries. Implement the coordinator, the durable participant transitions and a replacement's termination procedure. Your replay must give the same final decision to every shard whenever the recovery assumptions hold.

title: Consistent hashing · plan a live replica handoff
summary: A storage cluster is adding and removing virtual nodes while keys remain live. Build its placement service and a handoff planner. An operator must know exactly which ranges need copying, which replicas can retire, and which machine will answer each read.

title: Build a Redis-compatible TCP server
summary: Two clients share a keyspace. One sends half a request and pauses. The other pipelines a SET and a GET containing a newline and a zero byte. Implement the server that decodes the stream, applies commands, and sends each reply to the right socket. Then connect two real clients to the same code on localhost.

title: Build a bounded message-schedule checker
summary: A payment handler occasionally credits the same request twice. The retry that triggers it never appears in sequential tests. Build the event explorer behind a distributed-systems test harness and return a shortest schedule that reproduces the double credit.

title: Commit MapReduce output under retries and speculation
summary: A slow worker keeps running after the scheduler starts a backup. Both send a completion; another worker reports success after its attempt expired. Build the coordinator for a word-count service so each logical map contributes exactly one output and readers only see a complete job. The trace lets you deliberately pick which worker finishes first.

title: Distributed snapshot · account for money in flight
summary: Two ledgers transfer credits over FIFO links. Recording both balances while payments are moving can make credits seem to disappear. Implement the Chandy–Lamport marker rules and channel recorder in the supplied transport simulator. Produce a consistent cut that an auditor can add up.

title: Reconcile an offline set with an observed-remove CRDT
summary: Two offline consoles edit the same set of machine labels. A console removes a label while a peer adds it again. After reconnecting, the network delivers a current update, then an older copy twice. Implement local edits and replica reconciliation so an old packet cannot resurrect a deleted tag and a concurrent add can survive.

title: SWIM membership · investigate a false suspicion
summary: A slow service answers a relayed ping just as a timeout fires. Later, stale gossip accuses the recovered process again. Implement the failure detector and incarnation-aware membership table at a single observer. Return the outgoing messages so an operator can distinguish a relayed success from a declaration of failure.

title: LSM storage engine · recover writes and compact tombstones
summary: A storage service occasionally resurrects deleted keys after its compactor runs. Implement the read path, log recovery, and range of runs selected for compaction. Replay writes across a crash and inspect the exact disk layout that results.

title: MVCC · implement snapshot isolation and reproduce write skew
summary: Two on-call engineers each see the other person on duty and take themselves off call. Your transaction engine should reproduce that outcome under snapshot isolation, while rejecting two concurrent writers to the same key. Implement version selection and atomic commit, then use the replay trace to explain the difference.

title: Implement copy-on-write fork and page faults
summary: A worker forks immediately before reading a shared dataset. Eager copying doubles memory use, but sharing a writable page lets the child corrupt its parent. Finish the page-table clone and write-fault paths, then replay forks, writes, and exits against a reference-counted physical allocator.

title: Schedule interactive jobs with multilevel feedback queues
summary: A long batch job owns the CPU when an interactive job wakes up. Build an event-driven scheduler that reacts immediately, preserves CPU usage across interruptions, and occasionally restores priority. Its dispatch trace is the only evidence available when a job finishes late.

title: Build a forwarding trie and update IPv4 headers
summary: A router learns a specific subnet and later loses it. Packets should switch to the remaining covering route, leave with one fewer hop, and carry a consistent header checksum. Build the forwarding information base and connect it to the packet path.

title: Reassemble an out-of-order byte stream
summary: A file transfer delivers some bytes twice, some in the wrong order, and its end marker before a gap is filled. Implement the receive buffer that reconstructs exactly the byte sequence an application can read after each delivery.

title: Compile short-circuit expressions to a stack VM
summary: A rule engine charges for every variable lookup. A cached result should skip a backend lookup, yet an eager compiler still reads it and can crash on an unbound name. Implement the bytecode compiler and virtual machine. The access log must show exactly which reads ran.

title: Remove dead assignments across a control-flow graph
summary: A compiler deletes an accumulator that a loop reads on its next iteration. Its cleanup pass also keeps whole chains that feed a single unused value. Implement backward liveness and an optimizer over a small imperative IR, then run the optimized program in the supplied interpreter. An emitted event or a division error is observable even if the destination is never read.
